title: Different Demographic Cues Yield Inconsistent Conclusions About LLM Personalization and Bias
abstract: arXiv:2601.18486v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Demographic cue-based evaluation is widely used to study how large language models (LLMs) adapt their responses to signaled demographic attributes within and across groups. This approach typically relies on a single cue (e.g., names) as a proxy for group membership, implicitly treating different cues as interchangeable operationalizations of a single underlying identity-conditioned behavior. We test this assumption in realistic advice-seeking interactions spanning 14.8 million prompts, focusing on race and gender in a U.S. context. We find that cues for the same group induce only partially overlapping changes in model responses, yielding inconsistent conclusions about personalization, while bias conclusions are unstable, with both magnitude and direction of group differences varying across cues. We further show that these inconsistencies reflect differences in cue-group association strength and linguistic features bundled within cues

translated_title: 不同的人口统计线索导致关于大语言模型个性化与偏见的不一致结论
translated_abstract: 基于人口统计线索的评估方法被广泛用于研究大语言模型（LLM）如何根据所暗示的人口属性在群体内部和跨群体调整其回应。这种方法通常依赖于单一线索（如姓名）作为群体成员身份的代理，隐含地将不同线索视为单一潜在身份条件行为的可互换操作化。我们在涵盖1480万个提示的现实寻求建议交互中对这一假设进行了检验，聚焦于美国情境下的种族和性别。我们发现，指向同一群体的不同线索仅引起模型回应部分重叠的变化，导致关于个性化的结论不一致，而偏见结论也不稳定，群体差异的幅度和方向在不同线索之间存在变化。我们进一步表明，这些不一致反映了线索与群体关联强度的差异以及线索中捆绑的语言特征。
tldr: 该研究通过1480万个提示的大规模实验发现，使用不同人口统计线索评估大语言模型的个性化与偏见会得出不一致甚至矛盾的结论，证明单一线索（如姓名）不能作为群体身份的可靠代理，现有评估方法存在根本性缺陷。
en_tdlr: Through experiments spanning 14.8 million prompts, this study demonstrates that different demographic cues yield inconsistent conclusions about LLM personalization and bias, revealing that single-cue evaluations are unreliable and cues are not interchangeable proxies for group identity.
